game.title: Psychonauts
game.build_notes: Verified against the Steam build on Windows 10, 2026-08-27. Key bindings and level codes may differ on other releases.

api_notes: Polls the mouse with immediate-mode GetDeviceState on GUID_SysMouse (vtable slot 9). Confirmed by hooking the chain DirectInput8Create -> IDirectInput8::CreateDevice -> IDirectInputDevice8::GetDeviceState and seeing all three install.
Window-level SendInput with scancodes works for menus and gameplay, provided the game window is genuinely foreground.

Forging keyboard input at the DirectInput buffer / key-state level was tried and refuted twice on this game: the keyboard is not read via buffered GetDeviceData, and a correctly-forged polled-buffer press reaches the input state machine but the title screen does not consume it. Use window-level SendInput instead.
See UNIVERSAL.md on the shared-vtable trap before hooking any DirectInput device method here.

bindings.context: door prompts, menu selection, 'Press A to begin'
bindings.notes: This is the controller-A equivalent. The in-game prompts show a controller glyph, not a key.

bindings.action: confirm — does NOT work on door prompts
bindings.notes: Pressed repeatedly on a door prompt with no effect. SPACE is the action key. ENTER *does* select dialogue options, so it is not simply inert everywhere.

bindings.context: dialogue option list, menus, save-slot list
bindings.notes: Arrow keys MUST be sent as extended or DirectInput sees the numpad variant.

Movement is camera-relative. In the brain vault the camera orbits as the character walks, so the same key does not map to the same world direction twice. Hold ~300-600ms for a small step; taps often do nothing.
TOGGLES. It does NOT dismiss popups. Mistaking this for a dismiss key silently invalidated three experiments in one session — the Journal was open and the game was ignoring camera input.

bindings.context: figment / journal tutorial popups showing a 'B Exit' glyph
bindings.notes: PARTIALLY ESTABLISHED. One of X or C cleared it; which was not isolated because ESC was pressed in the same sequence. BACKSPACE (0x0E) definitely does NOT work. Worth pinning down — these popups block input and will stall an unattended run.

routes.goal: From the title screen to a loaded save game.

steps.note: Walk the character to the GREEN door. Arrow keys orbit the brain, so this cannot be a fixed key sequence — capture a screenshot between steps and steer. Yellow = New Game, blue = Continue, green = Load a Saved Game.

steps.expect_cue: on-screen prompt reads 'Press (A) to Load a Saved Game'
green notepad headed 'LOAD GAME' with numbered slots

steps.note: cursor starts on slot A; one DOWN reaches slot 1

steps.expect_cue: selection box around the intended slot

routes.notes: The brain-vault leg is the fragile part. It was completed once and then NOT reproducible an hour later from a different starting orientation, because the camera orbits with the character. Treat it as steer-with-feedback, not replay.

routes.goal: Load a save from inside gameplay, avoiding the brain vault entirely.

steps.note: menu order is CONTINUE / OPTIONS / LOAD / SAVE / QUIT TO TITLE / CREDITS

routes.notes: PROBABLY THE BEST ROUTE and it is under-explored. The Journal also offers SAVE, so making one save in a convenient location removes the navigation problem permanently.

routes.goal: End a conversation and return to gameplay.

steps.note: repeat until the last option is selected — it is the polite exit line

saves.label: The Milkman Conspiracy — The Neighborhood
saves.notes: The open outdoor area. Prefer this over a level-code jump when an open space is needed.

level_codes.lands: Boyd's house INTERIOR — enclosed rooms, not the street
level_codes.notes: The name suggests the Milkman level; it is an interior. Jumping here to reach the open neighbourhood wasted a large part of a session.

level_codes.lands: an underground sanctuary — the NPC there is Ford Cruller
level_codes.notes: Catalogued elsewhere as 'Sasha's Lab' from a loading-screen filename match, which the actual content contradicts. Treat filename-derived level labels as hypotheses. A level jump also runs the level's opening script, so it can land mid-cutscene or mid-dialogue rather than in free control.

entry_points.notes: Level-code jumps load a level fresh and do NOT restore save progress.

hazards.description: Figment and journal tutorial popups take over input until dismissed, and can appear from ordinary play such as collecting a figment.
hazards.impact: Stalls unattended automation; also silently invalidates tests because the game stops responding to camera input.

hazards.description: The Journal was observed open at the start of tests where no key had been sent.
hazards.impact: Three consecutive camera experiments produced meaningless results.
hazards.root_cause: In that session it was self-inflicted — a DirectInput hook corrupting the keyboard state array and synthesising Escape (see UNIVERSAL.md). Whether the game also opens it on its own is unestablished.
hazards.mitigation: Verify state visually immediately before every test.

hazards.description: Camera does not respond to mouse-look or to camera memory writes while a menu is open.
hazards.impact: Produces false negatives that look like technical failure.
